analysis:
Unit 11 (head lines 485-675) is unchanged context according to the complete range map; changed head ranges in this file start at line 923. It was still checked against T-041: the prefix-cache, KEK, TTL and LaunchAgent passthrough text is consistent with the canonical posture, including DEBUG-only DARKBLOOM_DEBUG_CACHE_KEY_FILE at line 691 and the TTL max of 1800 at line 692. Nothing is new there.

Unit 12 has the change at head lines 923-949, the Cluster runtime facts section. It newly states that a signed release registers `cluster_runtime` in POST /v1/releases, gated by an environment variable. The coordinator then derives that build's cluster approvals, pair-serving grants and parity qualifications from the block, and operator copying becomes optional. The new `--release-candidates` mode (lines 941-948) describes catalog models. Line 945 adds that an artifact the worker describes only as another registered model is left out.

This moves pair-serving authority onto the release-publication credential (A-005). It sits in tension with A-017/T-054, which keep qualifications separate from publication, and the threat model has no entry for it. That is reported as a low threat-model-gap finding. It rests on documentation of platform-owned backend behavior that is not verified here.

Open question for integration: whether patches in other batches (provider-release.md, ClusterRuntimeApprovalFacts.swift, the provider-side check of served approvals) show the provider treating a coordinator-served approval as sufficient. Also whether the platform requires independent qualification approval for derived parity qualifications. Remaining changed ranges at head lines 954-1015, 1077-1104 and 1631-1636 are outside these units.

findings.detail: Head lines 923-931 now say a signed release's POST /v1/releases payload may carry a `cluster_runtime` block. A coordinator that accepts it derives that build's cluster approvals, pair-serving grants and parity qualifications. Before, an operator copied the digests into the operator approval file. So the release-registration credential (A-005) and release publication now decide pair-serving permission, not only binary-hash trust (A-011). The threat model keeps durable qualifications independently approved and separate from release publication (A-017, T-054), and TB-011/T-052 deny serving permission to evidence that is not an authorization. None of these entries covers cluster-pair grants derived from release payloads. Trigger: anyone who can register a release, or a compromised release lane, publishes cluster_runtime digests for an unqualified helper or worker. Members whose local facts match would then be offered a pair (lines 931-936). This is a documentation claim about platform-owned backend behavior and was not verified here. Fix: add the cluster_runtime release path to the threat model (A-005/A-017/T-054). State whether derived parity qualifications stay separate from release-key authority and need independent approval. Confirm the platform enforces that separation.
findings.title: Release registration now said to derive cluster approvals, pair-serving grants and parity qualifications; threat model lacks this path
